scope: Committed alarms, signed outbox/inbox requests and durable receiver receipts, replicated conditional settlement, capability gates, immutable Blob closure and an executable producer/receiver primary-replacement/retained-disk restart drill. Full unit and owning integration regressions at one frozen source.
environment: macOS native Rust Node/SDK/SQLite/LTX/Raft Engine/TLS. Two independent three-voter clusters exercise delivery races; three-voter groups exercise alarms. Explicit single-voter development fixtures exercise Blob closure and self-delivery; unsupported-factory cases create no Raft engine/catalog. The process drill uses three real local Node instances/two groups and the persistent development Bucket object-store adapter. Integration stores use real conditional in-memory operations. No cellar_internal_tests.
limitations: All 782 unique unit/integration cases identified by target/name across 21 binaries pass at this source, plus four compile-fail SDK capability doctests and a two-process producer/receiver restart drill; all 34 recorded commands pass. Nine ignored child entry points run through owning parents and are excluded from totals. All six original MR-12 requirements are present and pass. A held private emission produces zero sends; rollback retains the prior settled prefix. The leadership race observes committed receiver state while its S3 response is held, replaces the source primary, requires a new identical request/ID, then verifies one receiver mutation and replicated settlement. The lost-completion case blocks source archive after receiving actual receiver proof, observes committed settlement below S3 coverage, closes the primary with a nonempty ambiguous-command report, and recovers the settled prefix without another send. This is native receiver idempotency, not a generic external exactly-once guarantee or Byzantine certificate. Requests and receipts bind full histories, stable target definition plus exact operation contract, keys, policy and actual payload. Immutable namespace roots still check the full compiled manifest; definition identities permit self/cyclic declarations without recursive hashes. Native self-delivery is qualified with one explicit development voter; multi-voter cross-cluster delivery has separate cases. Normal receiver operations cannot consume delivery clients; altered inputs and insufficient receipt policy refuse, equal and older retained retries return exact stored receipts, and later lane sequences reuse one client. Alarms and outbox share one internal allocator, scheduler and precharged metadata; priority alternates per history. Public Node-first cancellation still joins its timer domain, but its existing Fleet outcome does not provide a graceful Raft close receipt/archive obligations. MR-13 must unify that contract, role readiness, metrics and safe receipt maintenance. Existing receipt limits apply with no automatic pruning, latest-receiver retention/pruning API or unlimited-duration/outage claim. Permanently refused deliveries remain retained and block their lane; no implicit payload rewrite or dead-letter/skip operation. Physical SQL can delay the single scheduler; no latency SLO is established. Keys/grants/limits/protocol identities enter class compatibility; normal classes preserve prior identity. Prototype diagnostic failures below are retained with honest source notes, not treated as qualification of an uncommitted tree. The restart drill resumes retained disks and a persistent development object store, with explicit demo identities/keys. No physical Amazon S3, machine power loss, independent physical zones, production performance/capacity, 24-hour soak, 30/100/1000-node tiers, federation or complete release is claimed. MR-13 through MR-17 remain open. Existing vendored warnings remain visible.
